description: The ear's test: short sounds made while Stand is speaking, some of them someone calling for it and some not. Until 2026-11-15 none of them stopped Stand, because a sound had to be loud for 0.6 seconds to count as someone speaking: a person said "excuse me" and "hello" five times before a whole sentence got through. A line here says what should become of it: "stops" for a call (a person's own "hello" and "excuse me" from that day, and "wait" in one of the Mac's voices), "passes" for everything else ("yeah", "right", a real laugh, and "you go ahead" said to someone else). The last line is a whole sentence, which stops Stand the ordinary way. After each call someone says what they wanted, as a person does once they have the speaker's attention. What to read in the report: the last column of "What the audience did", and the table "The ear". Run it several times, and with --no-ear to see the fault: every short line passes. It needs the recordings runs/2026-11-13T16-20-06-gemini-app and runs/2026-11-15T18-43-13-gemini-app, which are never published, so it runs only on the Mac that has them. Lines are timed by how long Stand has spoken. A line that happens to land as a section ends is not the ear's case: Stand has stopped by itself and hears the word as it would in any silence.

during.label: says what they wanted
during.say: Sorry, what is your name again?

during.label: a short laugh
during.say: (a laugh of two seconds, not loud)

during.label: says what they wanted
during.say: Could you say that last part once more?

during.label: says "you go ahead" to someone else
during.say: (you go ahead, to the other person in the room)

during.label: calls for it (a person's own "excuse me")
says what they wanted
during.say: How much does an hour of it cost?

during.label: asks in a whole sentence
during.say: Sorry, one more thing. Can it join a call by itself?

goodbye.label: goodbye
goodbye.say: Thanks, that's all the questions we have.
